02 / 18

Framing

Accuracy is the wrong instrument for this question.

Compression is not a research condition — it is what happens to every clip in every deployed pipeline. The question is not whether a lossy codec costs a model some points. It is whether the model, handed the same spoken content in a different container, still reaches its answer from the same acoustic evidence.

Two models can score identically and disagree completely about why. A benchmark that reports only accuracy cannot see that, and cannot warn you about it.

This is why the classifier here is a decision tree, a forest, a boosted ensemble, an SVM and a small neural net over named acoustic features — not an end-to-end black box. Every unit of evidence has an acoustic name, so "what moved" is answerable in the vocabulary of speech science.

Does MP3 change the model's mind, or just its evidence?

The question03 / 18

Literature review · 1 of 3

Codecs degrade speech models. That part is settled.

Corpus

Cao, H., Cooper, D. G., Keutmann, M. K., Gur, R. C., Nenkova, A., & Verma, R. (2014). CREMA-D: Crowd-sourced emotional multimodal actors dataset. IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing, 5(4), 377–390.

The corpus paper. 7,442 clips, 91 actors, 12 fixed sentences, crowd-rated by 2,443 raters. Reports human recognition from audio alone at 40.9% — the number that keeps this task honest.

Codec

Reddy, A. P., & Vijayarajan, V. (2020). Audio compression with multi-algorithm fusion and its impact in speech emotion recognition. International Journal of Speech Technology, 23(2), 277–285.

Establishes the baseline expectation: compression costs SER accuracy, and the cost is feature-dependent rather than uniform. Licenses an expectation, not a prediction — and says nothing about explanations.

Codec

Wu, H., Chen, X., Lin, Y.-C., … Lee, H. (2024). Codec-SUPERB @ SLT 2024: A lightweight benchmark for neural audio codec models (arXiv:2409.14085).

The methodological anchor: signal-level fidelity metrics do not capture losses in paralinguistic content. You cannot infer behavioural damage from SNR or PESQ — you have to measure behaviour separately.

Standards

Kapoor, S., Cantrell, E. M., Peng, K., … Narayanan, A. (2024). REFORMS: Consensus-based recommendations for machine-learning-based science. Science Advances, 10(18).

Adopted as the reporting standard — hence the speaker-independent splits, the recorded encoder arguments, and the per-stage attrition counts later in this deck.

All references verified against Crossref DOI records or the arXiv API.

Literature04 / 18

Literature review · 2 of 3

The toolkit: attribution by perturbation, and its known limits.

Method

Ribeiro, M. T., Singh, S., & Guestrin, C. (2016). "Why should I trust you?": Explaining the predictions of any classifier. KDD '16, 1135–1144.

LIME. A model can be probed purely by perturbing inputs and watching outputs — the licence under which any of this is possible on an opaque model.

Method

Lundberg, S. M., & Lee, S.-I. (2017). A unified approach to interpreting model predictions (arXiv:1705.07874). NeurIPS 2017.

SHAP's additive framework and consistency axioms. Used here as the primary global attribution — exact via TreeSHAP for the ensembles, and, as slide 21 shows, badly behaved when sampled.

Method

Zeiler, M. D., & Fergus, R. (2014). Visualizing and understanding convolutional networks. ECCV 2014, 818–833.

The origin of occlusion sensitivity: mask part of the input, watch the output move. Our feature-neutralisation test is this method on the feature axis.

Audio

Haunschmid, V., Manilow, E., & Widmer, G. (2020). audioLIME: Listenable explanations using source separation (arXiv:2008.00582).

Interpretability for audio must mean listenability; spectrogram patches are not audible objects. Our answer is to make every feature an acoustician's quantity — F0, jitter, CPPS, band energy — rather than a pixel region.

Audio

Nasr, S., Ren, Z., & Johnson, D. (2025). Beyond saliency: Enhancing explanation of speech emotion recognition with expert-referenced acoustic cues (arXiv:2511.11691).

Saliency imported from vision highlights regions without showing they are meaningful acoustic markers. The direct argument for expert-referenced features.

Audio

Sotirou, T., Lyberatos, V., Menis Mastromichalakis, O., & Stamou, G. (2024). MusicLIME: Explainable multimodal music understanding (arXiv:2409.10496).

Attribution can reveal which information channel a model leans on — the same move we make between voice evidence and codec artefact.

Literature05 / 18

Literature review · 3 of 3 · load-bearing

Explanations are fragile, and they can lie convincingly.

Core

Ghorbani, A., Abid, A., & Zou, J. (2019). Interpretation of neural networks is fragile (arXiv:1710.10547). AAAI 2019.

Perceptually indistinguishable inputs, given the same predicted label — sometimes with higher confidence — receive substantially different interpretations. The accuracy/explanation dissociation, established in vision under adversarially constructed perturbation.

Core

Adebayo, J., Gilmer, J., Muelly, M., Goodfellow, I., Hardt, M., & Kim, B. (2018). Sanity checks for saliency maps (arXiv:1810.03292). NeurIPS 2018.

Some widely used saliency methods are independent of the model and the data — plausible pictures that explain nothing, and the eye cannot tell. Any claim that an explanation moved must first prove the explanation was real.

Ghorbani needed an adversary. A transcode is not an adversary — it is Tuesday.

Literature06 / 18

The gap

Three literatures that have not been introduced.

Established Codec robustness is measured on task-specific models, and reported as an accuracy delta.
Established XAI for audio is developed on clean corpora, where the format is never a variable.
Established Explanation fragility is shown under adversarial perturbation, in vision.

Nobody has asked what an ordinary MP3 encode does to a model's explanation.

So the design is: hold the spoken content fixed, vary only the container, and measure the attribution — across six model families and ten explainability methods, with Adebayo's sanity check run first so that a moving explanation means something.

Positioning07 / 18

Dataset

CREMA-D: fixed sentences, acted emotion, crowd-rated.

Twelve fixed sentences spoken by 91 actors in six emotions. The fixed lexicon is the reason this corpus suits the question: linguistic content is held constant, so acoustic effects can be isolated from what is being said.

Class balance1,271 each; NEU 1,087

Dataset08 / 18

Dataset · label quality

The ceiling is low, and that is the honest context.

Hearing audio alone, CREMA-D's crowd matched the actor's intended emotion in 45.5% of clips in our recomputation from the voice-only vote tabulation. Recall is wildly uneven: neutral 0.97 and anger 0.67, but sadness 0.16 — listeners fall back on "neutral" when acted affect is subtle.

Consequence for this study: absolute accuracy is not a meaningful measure of "emotion recognition" here, which is a further reason to put the weight on attribution.

Dataset09 / 18

Preprocessing · design

One canonical reference, then a controlled chain.

Every condition descends from the same normalised source, so any downstream difference is attributable to the codec and nothing else — not to loudness, sample rate, or channel count.

Source
CREMA-D WAV
7,442 clips pulled from the corpus' git-lfs media endpoint.
Condition · ref
16 kHz mono PCM16
EBU R128 loudness-normalised (I=-23, LRA=7, TP=-2). The lossless reference.
Condition · mp3_64
MP3 @ 64 kbps
libmp3lame, encoded from ref. The primary contrast.
Condition · mp4_aac64
MP4/AAC @ 64 kbps
Audio-only MP4, for a second codec at matched bitrate.
Control · roundtrip_wav
AAC decoded to WAV
Same codec output, different container — isolates container from codec.

Decoding is uniform: every stimulus, whatever its container, is decoded to float32 PCM through the same ffmpeg call. Letting soundfile read the WAVs and audioread the MP3s would confound the codec effect with the decoder.

Preprocessing10 / 18

Feature engineering

436 columns, every one with an acoustic name.

Frame-level contours are reduced to eight order statistics — mean, SD, min, max, median, IQR, skew, kurtosis — so the result is a plain tabular dataset a decision tree can consume and a phonetician can read.

spectral_* · 114 Centroid, bandwidth, rolloff 85/95%, flatness, flux, entropy, slope, ZCR, RMS, 7-band contrast, 8 band-energy ratios, and explicit high-frequency survival ratios above 4 and 6 kHz. Why: this is the family a lossy codec attacks first.
mfcc_* · 240 20 MFCCs with Δ and ΔΔ; full statistics on the static coefficients, mean and SD on the derivatives. Why: the standard SER front end — included so results are comparable to the literature.
prosody_* · 56 Praat F0 statistics and slope, jitter ×4, shimmer ×6, HNR, formants F1–F5 with bandwidths, intensity, voiced-segment timing, CPPS. Why: the source–filter view — where emotion actually lives, and what we expect a codec to leave alone.
chroma_* · 24 + 2 global 12 pitch classes, plus clip duration and peak amplitude. Note: chroma tuning is pinned to 0 — estimating it is a music operation, and an estimated tuning could itself shift under compression and confound the contrast.
Features11 / 18

Feature engineering · settings

The parameters, stated so the numbers can be reproduced.

AnalysisSetting
Sample rate / channels16 kHz · mono
FFT size512 (32 ms)
Window / hop400 (25 ms) / 160 (10 ms)
MFCC20 coefficients · 40 mel bands
Mel range20 – 8000 Hz
Praat pitch range75 – 500 Hz
Max formant / count5500 Hz · 5
Band edges (Hz)0·500·1k·2k·3k·4k·5k·6k·8k

The band edges are not arbitrary. The top two straddle the region where 64 kbps encoders begin discarding content, which makes those columns the most diagnostic features in the table — and, as it turns out, the most dangerous.

Two engineering notes worth recording. Praat's aggregate formant queries replace a per-frame Python loop — same numbers, ~50× fewer interpreter round trips. And librosa.estimate_tuning segfaulted on this machine, which is a second reason tuning is pinned rather than estimated.

Extraction: 29,768 files in 10 min 20 s on 10 workers.

Features12 / 18

EDA · 1 of 4 · table health and redundancy

Before any model: is the table sound?

No constant columns. Only 5 of 436 features contain any missing value, and one exceeds 1%: prosody_shimmer_apq11 at 11.3% — expected, since APQ11 needs eleven consecutive glottal periods and short or creaky clips do not supply them.

Heavy tails are mild: the worst feature has 0.89% of values beyond |z| > 5. Redundancy is contained — 49 pairs correlate above 0.95, 7 above 0.99, several of them Praat's own algebraic duplicates (jitter_rap vs jitter_ddp, r = 1.00). Mean absolute off-diagonal correlation: 0.18.

EDA13 / 18

EDA · 2 of 4 · what carries emotion

Emotion lives in the dynamics, not the levels.

397 of 436 features separate emotion at Bonferroni-corrected significance. The strongest are all variability measures — mfcc_d1_00_std (F = 1194), mfcc_00_std (F = 1159), prosody_intensity_std (F = 1078). Translated: how much the loudness moves carries more about acted emotion than any average level does.

Per feature, MFCCs are the weakest family by mutual information (0.061) despite holding 55% of the columns; chroma (0.098) and prosody (0.087) lead. MFCC dominance downstream is a matter of count, not quality — a point the attribution results return to.

EDA14 / 18

EDA · 3 of 4 · the confound that had to be handled

Speaker identity outweighs emotion in 340 of 436 features.

Mean variance explained: speaker η² = 0.178 against emotion η² = 0.098. Prosody (0.232) and chroma (0.254) are the most speaker-bound families of all.

This is why every split in the study partitions actors, never rows: 60 train / 11 validation / 20 test speakers, with no voice appearing on both sides.

A random row split would have measured voice recognition and called it emotion.

EDA15 / 18

EDA · 4 of 4 · structure

High-dimensional, and format is not a visible cluster.

51 principal components are needed for 95% of the variance (PC1 21.7%, PC2 8.2%) — the space is genuinely high-dimensional, not a few latent factors in disguise.

Note what the right-hand panels do not show: the format conditions sit on top of one another. At the level of gross geometry, an MP3 clip looks like its WAV original. The damage is not visible here — it is concentrated in a handful of directions, which is exactly why it took a paired, per-feature test to find.

EDA16 / 18

The signal · WAV vs MP3

The median feature is untouched. The tail is destroyed.

Across 436 features the median shift under MP3 is 0.020 SD — nothing. But 28 features move by more than half a standard deviation, and one moves by 38.6: spectral_contrast_6_mean, the 6–8 kHz band, goes from 16.4 to 46.4. Spectral flatness collapses alongside it as the encoder zeroes masked bins.

These are not degradations. They are the encoder's fingerprint.
